result.title: MemHand: Memory-Enhanced World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
result.summary: Recovering the continuous world-space motion of both hands from egocentric video is essential for applications such as human-to-robot policy transfer and augmented reality. Achieving this goes beyond reconstructing the hands from each individual frame, as the context that a frame needs is often spread over time, especially around occlusions or when a hand moves out of sight. Recent works have explored how to exploit temporal context, yet they mostly draw it from fixed-length windows. Such windows cannot guarantee that every frame has the context required to reconstruct the hands in world space with accurate poses and metric scale. To address this limitation, we introduce MemHand, a memory-enhanced framework for world-space hand motion reconstruction. MemHand maintains two complementary forms of memory. The Short-Term Event Memory keeps the context of the well-observed hand around each occlusion or out-of-sight event and supplies it to frames with weak or missing visual evidence. In addition, since the metric scale holds over the whole recording, the Long-Term Scale Memory retains the most reliable observations across the video as scale anchors within a bounded state. Across benchmarks featuring severe occlusions and frequent out-of-sight intervals, MemHand achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and generalizes well to unseen domains. Benefiting from the synergy of both memories, it cuts W-MPJPE by 57\% on ARCTIC and 70\% on HOT3D relative to StableHand, delivering continuous and metrically accurate world-space hand poses and trajectories. We will release our code and models at the project page: https://irmvlab.github.io/memhand.github.io

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MemHand，从第一人称视频重建双手连续的世界坐标运动：用短期事件记忆保存遮挡或手离开视野前后的上下文，并以长期尺度记忆在有界状态内保存最可靠的观测作为尺度锚点。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「有界记忆状态＋可靠观测筛选＋证据缺失时补全上下文」的设计，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据保留、筛选与工作区状态更新提供方法线索，可供核查写入与更新规则能否迁移到 latent 推理状态。
